name: Layer-Recovery and Thin-Coordinate Dichotomy
statement: For an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor $X$, let $\mathcal L(X)$ be its successful layer sets and let $\mathcal T(X)$ be the coordinates whose two projected sections each have exactly one word absent from the other. Exactly one of two alternatives holds. If $\mathcal T(X)\ne\varnothing$, then $E_{\max}(X)=\mathcal T(X)$ and $\mathcal L(X)=2^{\mathcal T(X)}\setminus\{\varnothing\}$; the largest presentation has two repair tips with antipodally punctured rows, and $X$ has exactly two one-concept extensions in the dismantlable ample class. If $\mathcal T(X)=\varnothing$, then either no successful layer set exists or $\mathcal L(X)=\{E_{\max}(X)\}$; in the latter case $|E_{\max}(X)|\ge2$, the presentation has at least three repair tips, and $X$ has at most one dismantlable-ample one-concept extension. Hence a cornered terminal obstruction with every coordinate thick and two distinct resolving extensions has no common-seed presentation.
proof: Inside a recovered presentation on $E$, the fibre for a proper nonempty sublayer set $D$ equals the repair tip times the face that fixes the remaining owner coordinates to their missing signs. Hence $D$ is successful exactly when every owner meeting $D$ contains all of $E\setminus D$. This can occur for a proper sublayer set exactly when there are two owners; then both owner supports are all of $E$ and every nonempty subset is successful. A singleton is successful exactly when its coordinate is thin. If a thin coordinate exists, it lies in the unique largest successful set, forces that presentation to have two owners, and all its nonempty subsets are successful; their singleton members identify the largest set with $\mathcal T(X)$. Without thin coordinates, any largest successful presentation has at least three owners and admits no proper successful subset. The resolving-tip theorem gives exactly two extensions in the first case and at most one in the second.
comments: The fixed regressions verify the complete successful-set families, thin coordinates, owner counts, repair counts, sublayer fibre formula, and inherited balanced coordinates on six obstruction constructions.
